parameters.content:
## ppwr-campaign-launch

Works out which items are in scope, mints one signed link per item, and moves each one to `invited`.

**The token**

`<campaign_item_id>.<expires_ms>.<signature>`

The signature is an HMAC-SHA256 over `<campaign_item_id>|<expires_ms>`, taken by the Crypto node with the `PPWR Token Secret` credential. The secret lives in n8n's credential store and is nowhere in this repo.

Only `sha256(token)` is stored. The token itself exists in the link and nowhere else, so a copy of the database does not hand anyone a working link.

Workflow 02 then checks two things: the signature, which proves we minted it, and the stored hash, which proves it is the current one. Reissue a link and the old one stops working.

**Sending** goes out one message per supplier, with all of their links in it. Forty items is one email.

`dry_run: true` mints, stores and transitions without sending, and returns the links so a launch can be rehearsed. Set it to false when you mean it.

A failed send is recorded against the vendor and the launch carries on. One bad address should not stop a campaign.

### Mint

One signed link per item. The Crypto node does the signing and the Code nodes only assemble strings, so the secret never passes through JavaScript.

nodes.name: Launch campaign (webhook)
nodes.notes: The Public API cannot execute a workflow, so this is how an integration test drives a launch.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes:
campaign_id      which campaign to launch
form_base_url    where the supplier form is published. Set this to your own instance;
                 the default is a placeholder and will produce links that go nowhere.
token_ttl_days   how long a link stays valid
dry_run          true mints and stores without sending

value.where: ={{ [ { field: 'campaign_id', op: 'eq', value: $json.campaign_id }, { field: 'state', op: 'eq', value: 'pending' } ] }}

nodes.name: Resolve items in scope
nodes.notes: Mode is 'each'. The default passes every input item into one sub-execution, and the store answers a single request per call, so anything after the first would be dropped and nothing said about it.

nodes.name: Hash token for storage
nodes.notes: Only the hash is stored. A leaked database does not hand anyone a working link.

nodes.name: Store token hash
nodes.notes: Mode is 'each'. The default passes every input item into one sub-execution, and the store answers a single request per call, so anything after the first would be dropped and nothing said about it.

value.transition: ={{ { campaign_item_id: $('Hash token for storage').item.json.campaign_item_id, from_state: 'pending', to_state: 'invited', event_type: 'invite_sent', actor: 'system', payload: { dry_run: $('Configuration').first().json.dry_run } } }}

nodes.name: Transition to invited
nodes.notes:
The state change and its event log row are written together by the store, so an invite cannot be recorded without a trail.

Mode is 'each'. The default passes every input item into one sub-execution, and the store answers a single request per call, so anything after the first would be dropped and nothing said about it.

nodes.name: Anything in scope?
nodes.notes: True means nothing was pending. The run still reports what it did.

nodes.name: Load packaging item
nodes.notes:
Soft: an item row that has gone missing must not kill a whole launch.

Mode is 'each'. The default passes every input item into one sub-execution, and the store answers a single request per call.

nodes.name: Load vendor
nodes.notes:
Soft: same reason.

Mode is 'each'. The default passes every input item into one sub-execution, and the store answers a single request per call.

nodes.name: Actually send?
nodes.notes: A dry run mints, stores and transitions, then stops here. Everything except the email.

nodes.name: Send invite
nodes.notes: One bad address must not kill a 200 item campaign, so the error output is a modelled outcome instead of a swallow.
